summary: Clancy Fire Tower in Algonquin Park, one of 15 lookouts of the Pembroke Forest Fire District and on 1963 and later maps; no readable source describes the site today.

facts.agency: Ontario Department of Lands and Forests (now the MNR)

evidence.supports: Location given as Basin Depot, Ontario
Appears on the 1963 Department of Lands and Forests Tower Detection System Map
evidence.quote: Appears on the Department of Lands and Forests Tower Detection System Map (1963).

evidence.supports: Appears on Pembroke topographic map 31F, 3rd ed. 1977 and 4th ed. 1996
evidence.quote: Appears on Pembroke topographic map 31F, 3rd ed., 1977 and in current 4th ed., 1996.

evidence.supports: A towerman lived at Bridgedam (per a book by Roderick MacKay)
evidence.quote: Towerman lived at Bridgedam (ref. Roderick MacKay: Spirits of the Little Bonnechere)

evidence.supports: Pembroke Forest Fire District founded in 1922 by the Department of Lands and Forests
evidence.quote: The Pembroke Forest Fire District was founded by Ontario's former Department of Lands and Forests (now the MNR) in 1922

evidence.supports: District headquarters in Pembroke; central location for 15 fire tower lookouts
evidence.quote: It was the central location for 15 fire tower lookouts, including the towers in Algonquin Park.
The headquarters for the district were housed in the town.

evidence.supports: Clancy is named among the 15 towers
evidence.quote: The 15 towers included: Wilberforce, Mt. Edna, Sherwood, Murchison, Preston, Clancy, Fitzgerald
a towerman would get the degree bearings from his respective tower and radio back the information to headquarters

evidence.supports: District towers to be phased out after aerial firefighting in the 1970s (district-wide statement)
evidence.quote: These towers would all be phased out after aerial fire fighting techniques were employed in the 1970s.

notes_for_editor: The brief had no local_unit for Clancy, so the story uses Algonquin Park and Basin Depot from the firelookout.ca entry. That entry gives no elevation, tower type, structure height or build year (all N/A), so the build date and the tower's own history are unknown. Membership in the Pembroke district is from Wikipedia's list of 15 towers, which is undated for each tower. The 'phased out' sentence is a district-wide statement, not one about Clancy; the story presents it as the district's fate, and the editor should keep that framing. The 1922 event is the district's founding date, not the tower's, so it is recorded only with that note. The 1970s phase-out is not logged as an event because the source gives no year. The Algonquin Park Fire Tower Trail (a replica cupola at the Visitor Centre on Highway 60) is a different site and no source links it to Clancy, so it is left out. Status and access are unknown; no source describes the site now.
